name: Shilajit
short: Lab tests found lead and arsenic above permitted limits in Indian and Pakistani samples; a review says use without known metal levels is unsafe. 28-day study, 25 men: no serious events.
text: A laboratory analysis of shilajit samples from India and Pakistan, the two kinds mostly sold globally, found toxic elements including lead and arsenic, along with aluminium, nickel and chromium, in amounts that exceeded the standard permissible limits, and detected mercury only in the Indian samples. A 2024 review reported that shilajit contains around 65 heavy metals, including toxic ones such as lead, arsenic, cadmium and mercury; reported levels were mostly below WHO and FDA limits, except in a few studies where higher levels were reported, and the review concludes that taking shilajit without knowing its metal levels is not safe and could pose serious health problems. An earlier review states that the safety of shilajit is well documented in animal and human studies but that relatively few well-controlled human studies have been done. In a 28-day open-label, single-arm pilot study in 25 healthy men taking shilajit resin, no serious adverse events were reported and liver, kidney and blood tests stayed within normal limits; there was no placebo group. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
